subject: Clarify what counts as logs — prompts, model outputs, and deletion process
messages:
From: John Miller <john.miller@acme-corp.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick Q on logs: what exactly is kept by default?

Hi Stephanie,

Our security team is running through the integration checklist and wants a plain-English answer to how Redwood treats 'logs' by default. Specifically:
- Do you retain raw prompts and model outputs for hosted API calls?
- Are embeddings or derived vectors stored, and if so for how long?
- What is the deletion process if we ask Redwood to remove a subset of historical requests?

We're on a Hosted account now and evaluating whether to move to Dedicated. Could you summarize the defaults and any differences by deployment type (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)? A short table would be great.

Thanks — John
John Miller
Security Lead, Acme Corp

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: John Miller <john.miller@acme-corp.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on logs: what exactly is kept by default?

Hi John — thanks for the clear questions. Short answer up-front, then a concise table and the deletion steps.

Short answer: For Hosted, we retain request/response logs (which include prompts and model outputs) by default for 30 days to support debugging and quality checks. Embeddings are stored only if the customer explicitly enables "persist embeddings"; when stored they’re retained for 90 days by default unless otherwise contracted. For Dedicated, default retention is configurable by contract (we commonly see 90 days). For Private (VPC/on-prem), Redwood does not retain customer request logs by default — retention is customer-managed.

Retention summary (defaults)
- Hosted API: request/response logs (prompts + outputs) — 30 days; embeddings persisted only if enabled — 90 days.
- Dedicated: default 90 days (configurable in the SLA).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): 0 days by Redwood default; customer controls logging and retention.

Deletion process (how to remove data)
1) Submit a ticket to support with the time range and sample request IDs or the user/account identifier.
2) We schedule a targeted deletion job; for Hosted, that job removes logs from the primary store and marks records for deletion from backups.
3) Backups are purged on a rolling schedule; full purging from backups can take up to 30 days after the deletion job completes.
4) For Dedicated, deletion is done per contract and may require coordination with your infra contact (we can provide a narrow SLA).
5) For Private, since data is customer-managed, Redwood will provide guidance and scripts if you want assistance, but we do not delete customer-managed logs unless agreed.

Notes / caveats
- Cached artifacts (prefix caches / KV caches) are treated separately; we can expire cache entries going forward but cannot retroactively remove generated tokens already used by clients.
- Audit logs and billing records may be retained longer for compliance; these are scoped and we can discuss minimization if needed.

I attached a short retention-summary PDF and the Acme-specific data request template. Let me know if you want this condensed into a one-page table for your security checklist.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, John Miller <john.miller@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on logs: what exactly is kept by default?

Hi all — adding a couple technical clarifications from the infra side:

- "Request/response logs" include the full request body (prompts and metadata) and the full model output by default for Hosted. These are stored encrypted at rest.
- Embeddings that are persisted are stored as vectors with an associated hash and are available to your account namespace only. We do not index or surface persisted embeddings across accounts.
- If Acme needs a stricter retention window for Hosted, we can offer a 7- or 14-day retention profile as a configurable option on the account; this requires a minor billing adjustment and a short onboarding change.
- Deletion jobs will return a ticket ID; please retain that ID for your audit trail. The job response includes the set of request IDs removed and a timestamp.

If you want, Marissa and I can draft a one-page security note you can attach to your internal risk assessment.

— Rishi

From: John Miller <john.miller@acme-corp.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-08-24T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on logs: what exactly is kept by default?

Stephanie / Rishi — this is very helpful, thanks. Couple of follow-ups:
1) Please confirm the API or portal path to open a deletion request (will do as part of audit).
2) Can you supply the expected SLA for a Hosted targeted deletion (we need it for our Control Owner to sign off)?
3) Can you confirm whether model-level fine-tuning data (if we were to provide it) is treated under the same retention rules or flagged separately?

If you can reply with those three items I can close the ticket on our end. Attaching our completed data request form.

Thanks — John
